pairs.begin: Not only did the central bank cut interest rates,
pairs.end: but it also eased the rules on lending to small firms.

pairs.begin: Had the government acted earlier,
pairs.end: the shortage of grain could have been avoided.

pairs.begin: The more heavily a nation depends on a single export,
pairs.end: the more vulnerable it becomes to sudden price falls.

pairs.begin: No sooner had the new tax been announced
pairs.end: than shopkeepers began raising their prices at once.

items.explanation: Each opening demands its own structure: "Not only did" needs "but ... also", the inverted "Had ... acted" needs "could have been", "The more ..." needs "the more ...", and "No sooner had" needs "than".

pairs.begin: Were the software to be released without further testing,
pairs.end: the team would regret its haste.

pairs.begin: The engineers worked through the night lest
pairs.end: the deadline be missed by even a single day.

pairs.begin: So rapidly has the technology advanced that
pairs.end: any device bought last year is already obsolete.

pairs.begin: Whereas the first model relied on a single processor,
pairs.end: its successor divides the work among several.

items.explanation: "Were ... to be released" needs a "would" result, "lest" needs a bare subjunctive verb, "So rapidly has ... that" needs a consequence of rapid advance, and "Whereas" needs a contrasting clause about the successor.

pairs.begin: The council decided to restore the old wetland rather than
pairs.end: abandon it to the builders as useless wasteland.

pairs.begin: The reservoir, whose
pairs.end: level has fallen steadily for a decade, now supplies far less water than the city requires.

pairs.begin: Unless emissions are reduced substantially within the next decade,
pairs.end: the damage to coastal ecosystems may prove irreversible.

pairs.begin: Hardly had the monsoon arrived when
pairs.end: the dry riverbed began to fill with muddy water.

items.explanation: "rather than" needs a bare verb phrase ("abandon it ..."), "whose" needs a noun it possesses ("level"), "Unless" in the present needs a "may prove" result, and "Hardly had ... when" needs a past event.

pairs.begin: The problem was so complex as to
pairs.end: defeat even the most gifted students in the class.

pairs.begin: Were it not for the generous scholarship,
pairs.end: she would never have continued her studies abroad.

pairs.begin: However carefully a test is designed,
pairs.end: it can never measure every aspect of ability.

pairs.begin: It was not until the results arrived that
pairs.end: the students realised how much they had forgotten.

items.explanation: "so complex as to" needs a bare infinitive, "Were it not for" needs a "would have" result, "However carefully" needs a general present statement, and "It was not until ... that" needs a past-tense clause.

pairs.begin: Not until the patient's fever subsided
pairs.end: did the doctors allow her to leave the ward.

pairs.begin: Regular exercise is beneficial, provided it
pairs.end: is not carried to the point of exhaustion.

pairs.begin: Whereas some illnesses announce themselves with obvious symptoms,
pairs.end: others progress silently for years before they are detected.

pairs.begin: The clinic, which
pairs.end: was founded to serve the poorest families, now treats thousands each year.

items.explanation: "Not until" at the start forces inversion ("did the doctors allow"), "provided it" needs a verb, "Whereas some ... others" needs the contrasting group, and "which" needs a verb phrase describing the clinic.

pairs.begin: The more the empire expanded,
pairs.end: the harder it became to govern its distant provinces.

pairs.begin: Having exhausted its treasury in prolonged wars,
pairs.end: the kingdom could no longer pay its soldiers.

pairs.begin: The scribes were so meticulous that
pairs.end: a single error was rarely found in their copies.

pairs.begin: Neither the king nor his ministers
pairs.end: were willing to listen to the farmers' complaints.

items.explanation: "The more" needs "the harder", the opening participle phrase needs a subject that did the exhausting (the kingdom), "so meticulous that" needs a result about the scribes' copies, and a plural subject "Neither ... nor his ministers" needs "were willing".

pairs.begin: Inflation erodes savings insofar as
pairs.end: the interest they earn fails to keep pace with rising prices.

pairs.begin: Had the merchants not diversified their trade,
pairs.end: the collapse of one market would have ruined them.

pairs.begin: Few consumers notice a small price rise, let alone
pairs.end: take to the streets in protest.

pairs.begin: So long as demand for bread remains steady,
pairs.end: producers have little reason to alter their output.

items.explanation: "insofar as" needs a limiting clause about savings, the inverted "Had ... not diversified" needs "would have ruined", "let alone" needs a bare verb phrase that is a stronger reaction, and "So long as" needs a present result about producers.

pairs.begin: The more people rely on digital maps,
pairs.end: the less they trust their own sense of direction.

pairs.begin: Scarcely had the first reviews appeared when
pairs.end: the new novel was sold out in every bookshop.

pairs.begin: Provided the battery is charged overnight,
pairs.end: the latest model runs for days without a break.

pairs.begin: The council banned vehicles from the old quarter so as to
pairs.end: protect the fragile buildings from vibration.

items.explanation: "The more" needs "the less", "Scarcely had ... when" needs a past event, "Provided" needs a present result that depends on charging, and "so as to" needs a bare verb of purpose.
